summary.text: Emmer is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 6th District, first elected in 2014, and serves as House Majority Whip. A former trial attorney and Minnesota state representative, he was the Republican nominee for governor in 2010 and chaired the National Republican Congressional Committee from 2019 to 2023. He sits on the Committee on Financial Services, where he is Vice Chair.

paragraphs.text: Born in South Bend, Indiana, in 1961, and later moved with his family to Edina, Minnesota; graduated from St. Thomas Academy in Mendota Heights, Minnesota.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Alaska in 1984, where he played hockey, and a law degree from William Mitchell College of Law in 1988.

Practiced as a trial attorney, beginning by representing cities and counties through the League of Minnesota Cities Insurance Trust and the League of Minnesota Counties Insurance Trust, and later founded his own law firm; he is licensed in Minnesota, North Dakota and Wisconsin.
Served on the Independence City Council (1995-2002) and the Delano City Council (2003-2004).
Won election to the Minnesota House of Representatives (District 19B) in 2004 and served from 2005 to 2011, winning re-election in 2006 and 2008.

Ran for governor of Minnesota in 2010 rather than seeking a fourth House term; he won the Republican primary and lost the general election to Democrat Mark Dayton by less than half a percentage point.

Won the U.S. House seat for Minnesota's 6th District in 2014, succeeding Michele Bachmann, and took office in January 2015; he has served on the Committee on Financial Services throughout his time in Congress.
Chaired the National Republican Congressional Committee from January 2019 to January 2023, and became House Majority Whip on January 3, 2023.
In October 2023, after the removal of Speaker Kevin McCarthy, House Republicans voted to nominate Emmer for Speaker on October 24; he withdrew about four hours later.
